claims.text: A change breaks a client when a request that used to work now fails, or a response loses or changes something the client reads: removing or renaming a field, changing a field's type, or making an optional request field required.
claims.source_hint: outline item 1 of backend.l2.breaking-changes (curriculum definition; glossary breaking-change)

claims.text: At stage-1, DonHang.Api/Dtos.cs lines 5-9 declare ProductDto(int Id, string Name, int PriceVnd), OrderItemDto(int ProductId, int Quantity, int UnitPriceVnd) and OrderDto(int Id, int CustomerId, string Status, DateTimeOffset PlacedAt, List<OrderItemDto> Items).
ASP.NET Core's web defaults serialize each DTO property with a camelCase name, so PriceVnd is written as priceVnd and a property renamed to Price would be written as price.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Web API JSON serialization defaults (JsonSerializerDefaults.Web, camelCase naming policy)

claims.text: At stage-1, Product.fromJson in DonHang.App/lib/models.dart reads json['id'] as int, json['name'] as String and json['priceVnd'] as int from a Map<String, dynamic>.
In Dart, the [] operator of a Map returns null for a key that is not in the map, and casting null with `as int` (non-nullable) throws a TypeError at run time.
claims.source_hint: Dart API docs Map.operator []; Dart language docs, type tests and casts (as) under sound null safety

claims.text: Casting a JSON string value (decoded by jsonDecode as a Dart String) with `as int` throws, so sending priceVnd as "1250000" instead of 1250000 breaks Product.fromJson.
claims.source_hint: Dart API docs dart:convert jsonDecode (JSON strings become String); Dart language docs, type casts (as)

claims.text: At stage-1, ApiClient.fetchProducts maps every decoded item through Product.fromJson inside one async method, so an exception from one item makes the whole returned Future fail.

At stage-1, POST /api/v1/orders answers with an OrderDto (id, customerId, status, placedAt, items); OrderResult.fromJson in models.dart reads json["id"] as int and json["status"] as String and nothing else.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang OrdersController.cs Create (CreatedAtAction(..., ToDto(order))), ApiClient.createOrder and models.dart OrderResult at tag stage-1

claims.text: Adding a field to a response is not a breaking change for a client that reads only the fields it knows by name, because every existing name and type stays in place.
claims.source_hint: outline item 3 of backend.l2.breaking-changes; follows from Map lookup by key in Product.fromJson/OrderResult.fromJson

claims.text: The server cannot see which response fields each client reads, so a change counts as breaking if any existing client could rely on what it removes or changes.
Against the running stage-1 lab, curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products/1 prints {"id":1,"name":"Bàn phím cơ","priceVnd":1250000}.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang stage-1 lab (seed data db/, Caddyfile /api/v1/* proxy); same output as approved backend.l1.dtos-and-serialization Try it
